title.value: On the Spectral Bias of Neural Networks
title.justification: The title was mentioned at the beginning of the paper and matches the research context.
title.quote: On the Spectral Bias of Neural Networks

analysis.description: This paper investigates the learning bias of deep neural networks towards low frequency functions using Fourier analysis. It shows that ReLU networks exhibit a frequency-dependent learning speed, learning lower frequencies more robustly and faster than higher ones, even in lower-dimensional complex manifolds. The study highlights the spectral bias of neural networks in the context of their expressivity and parameterization.

type.justification: The paper provides a theoretical analysis of neural networks' learning behaviors using Fourier analysis, without focusing on empirical experiments.
type.quote: In this work, we present properties of neural networks that complement this aspect of expressivity. By using tools from Fourier analysis, we highlight a learning bias of deep networks.

name.justification: The paper discusses the spectral bias and learning behaviors in neural networks, which are core components of Deep Learning research.
name.quote: The remarkable success of deep neural networks at generalizing to natural data is at odds with the traditional notions of model complexity...

name.justification: The paper specifically discusses properties, learning biases, and Fourier analysis of neural networks, particularly ReLU networks.
name.quote: By using tools from Fourier analysis, we highlight a learning bias of deep networks towards low frequency functions.

name.justification: The core analytical method used in this paper is Fourier analysis to investigate the learning trends and biases of neural networks.
name.quote: We expose this bias by taking a closer look at neural networks through the lens of Fourier analysis.

name.justification: The paper introduces the concept of spectral bias as the tendency of neural networks to prioritize low-frequency functions during learning.
name.quote: ...we find that these networks prioritize learning the low frequency modes, a phenomenon we call the spectral bias.

name.justification: The paper uses ReLU networks as a primary model for investigating spectral bias and learning patterns.
name.quote: We focus the discussion on networks with rectified linear unit (ReLU) activations, whose continuous piece-wise linear structure enables an analytic treatment.

is_contributed.justification: ReLU networks are standard models used for the analysis and were not contributed as a new model by this paper.

is_executed.justification: The paper describes experiments using ReLU networks to explore their learning behaviors with respect to frequency.
is_executed.quote: We now present experiments showing that networks tend to fit lower frequencies first during training.
